rater.name: Draft answer key (written by Claude; Jeff to check)

criteria.reason: Mentions monsoons but not their seasonal change or how merchants planned around them.
criteria.quote: Monsoons were important for sailing.

criteria.reason: Two technologies with functions.
criteria.quote: Compasses showed which way was north even at night

criteria.reason: Connects bigger ships to more trade, but not the winds.
criteria.quote: Ships carrying more cargo made each voyage worth more

criteria.reason: Explains the seasonal reversal and using it for the outward and return trips.
criteria.quote: came home when it reversed

criteria.reason: Two technologies, each with what it did: direction and cargo.
criteria.quote: could carry much more cargo

criteria.reason: Links predictable voyages and bigger loads to trade growing and reaching more ports.
criteria.quote: Because voyages were more predictable and each ship carried more, trade grew

criteria.reason: Contradicts itself: the winds always blow one way, yet change. Ask the student which they mean.
criteria.quote: always blew toward India, but merchants waited for the winds to change

criteria.reason: Two technologies with functions: direction and cargo.
criteria.quote: larger ships held more spices and cloth

criteria.reason: Connects bigger ships to more goods, but not the winds.
criteria.quote: That meant more goods could be traded.

criteria.reason: Seasonal winds set when to leave and when to return.
criteria.quote: told merchants when to start their journeys and when to come back

criteria.reason: Both functions are wrong: the astrolabe estimated latitude, and a compass shows direction.
criteria.quote: the compass made the ship go faster

criteria.reason: Connects the winds to dependable voyages and trade; the technology link is wrong.
criteria.quote: Planning trips around the winds made voyages more dependable, which increased trade.

criteria.reason: Explains waiting for the winds to turn to make the return trip.
criteria.quote: waiting months for the winds to turn so they could return

criteria.reason: Explains one technology well; the question asks for two.
criteria.quote: The astrolabe helped sailors figure out how far north or south they were

criteria.reason: Connects a reliable schedule and navigation to more trips.
criteria.quote: merchants made more trips across open water

criteria.reason: Uses the seasonal pattern to time leaving and returning.
criteria.quote: leave Arabia in summer and return in winter

criteria.reason: Names two technologies without explaining either.
criteria.quote: They used compasses and astrolabes.

criteria.reason: A causal chain: wind timing, fewer losses, more goods sent.
criteria.quote: fewer ships were lost, so merchants were willing to send more goods

criteria.reason: About overland Silk Road trade; the monsoon winds are not mentioned.
No maritime technology.
Explains land trade, not Indian Ocean trade.
Treats the monsoon as rain, not as seasonal winds for planning voyages.
criteria.quote: Monsoons brought heavy rain

criteria.reason: Names two technologies but says nothing about what either did.
criteria.quote: used the astrolabe and the compass

criteria.reason: States that trade grew with no cause and effect.
criteria.quote: This made trade bigger.

criteria.reason: Seasonal reversal used for outward and return voyages.
criteria.quote: catch the opposite monsoon home

criteria.reason: Lateen sail and astrolabe, each with what it allowed.
criteria.quote: the astrolabe let navigators estimate latitude far from land

criteria.reason: Links timing, sailing and navigation to reaching farther ports and a wider network.
criteria.quote: merchants could reach farther ports more safely, so the network of trade grew wider

criteria.reason: Seasonal change in direction used to plan round trips.
criteria.quote: planned round trips around them

criteria.reason: Explains the lateen sail, but gives the compass no function and a wrong origin (it came from China).
criteria.quote: Europeans invented the compass

criteria.reason: Says trade grew without explaining how these causes produced it.
criteria.quote: These things made trade grow.
